examples.text: Herbert Propst.
Der Propst ist für die Hauptaufgaben in unserem Dom zuständig.
examples.translation: Le prieur est responsable des tâches principales de notre cathédrale.

glosses: der erste Würdenträger einer geistlichen Körperschaft

examples.text: Der Propst ist für die Hauptaufgaben in unserem Dom zuständig.
In einem Kirchenseminar werden aktuelle Probleme der Kirche von den Pröpsten behandelt.
Die Wohnung von Pröpsten bezeichnet man auch als Propstei.
„Dem Propst unterstanden auch die angrenzenden benachbarten Pfarrbezirke Wallersheim, Arzheim, Ems und Braubach (…).“
„Erster Präses des Konvikts war der spätere Propst und Bischöfliche Kommissarius Stübe (bis 1929).“

glosses: One placed in charge: a head, a chief
A dean: the head of a cathedral chapter.
One placed in charge: a head, a chief
The head of various other ecclesiastical bodies, even (rare, obsolete) muezzins.
One placed in charge: a head, a chief
The minister of the chief Protestant church of a town or region in Germany, the Low Countries, and Scandinavia.
One placed in charge: a head, a chief
The head of various colleges and universities.
One placed in charge: a head, a chief
One placed in charge: a head, a chief

A mayor: the chief magistrate of a town, particularly (Scotland) the head of a burgh or (historical) the former chiefs of various towns in France, Flanders, or (by extension) other Continental European countries.

examples.text: The repairs were completed in the summer of last year, more than ten months after the line had been closed, and the branch was re-opened on June 29, when Mr. T. F. Cameron, Chief Regional Officer, Scottish Region, received Provost J. S. Collin, of Eyemouth, at the station. The 12.42. p.m. train to Burnmouth was signalled out of the station by the Provost, after he had been introduced to the crew.

glosses: A senior deputy administrator; a vice-president of academic affairs.

examples.text: The provost of the University of Massachusetts has reversed a decision by faculty personnel committees not to renew the contracts of two professors engaged in sex research.

The princess, already a serious and diligent child, was given lessons on constitutional matters by Sir Henry Marten, the provost of Eton, and became aware even then that she should not show emotion and must maintain a certain reserve.

glosses: A steward or seneschal: a medieval agent given management of a feudal estate or charged with collecting fees.
A title of the archangel Michael.
Any manager or overseer in a medieval or early modern context.
The head of various Roman offices, such as prefect and praetor.
A constable: a medieval or early modern official charged with arresting, holding, and punishing criminals.

examples.text:
Here comes Signor Claudio, led by the provost
to prison;

glosses: An officer of the military police, particularly provost marshal or provost sergeant.
A provost cell: a military cell or prison.
To be delivered to a provost marshal for punishment.

examples.text: Around the time of the Rebellions of 1837 and the First Anglo-Afghan War, British servicemen spoke of being provosted.

translations.source_sense_description: Religion, katholische Kirche: der erste Würdenträger einer geistlichen Körperschaft

examples.text: Quant au moine, Gurth le reconnut à l’instant même pour le prieur de l’abbaye de Jorvaulx.
Wary de Dommartin la rebâtit ; d'abord bénédictin au monastère de Saint-Epvre à Toul, puis prieur de Varangéville, il céda ensuite son prieuré, moyennant redevance, à Jean de Nicolinis.

glosses: Titre de dignité dans quelques sociétés.

examples.text: Prieur de Sorbonne, de la maison de Sorbonne.
Brahim prend le parti d'étendre le verset qui parle "d'Allah qui prie pour Mahomet" vers une communication ... ça sous-entend qu'il y aura un prieur et un prié.
